title: Verification pass 2026-10-28: six figures published, the Medicare Bridge confirmed, every Lilly property still unread
summary: The verification pass of 2026-10-29, run end to end. The federal TrumpRx platform, medicare.gov, novocare.com, ozempic.com, aspe.hhs.gov, fda.gov, cms.gov and investor.lilly.com were read directly, and the Eli Lilly pages were read in a browser after our automated requests to them were refused. Twenty-one of forty-seven figures are now confirmed against a primary source, two remain conflicting and twenty-four remain unverified. Six figures that rendered no price now do, the Zepbound prices are filed per strength so that a dose can no longer inherit another dose price, the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge is confirmed at fifty dollars per month, and four of the five pending eligibility rules were retired against verbatim quotes. The figures whose conditions change on 2026-12-31 are staged on a separate branch and are not applied here.
changes: Wegovy injection, standard doses, TrumpRx: no published figure to $349 per month for the 1 mg, 1.7 mg and 2.4 mg strengths. Read 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/wegovy, which states that this price applies from the first fill and is not a figure that follows a promotional period.

Foundayo, TrumpRx: no published figure to $149 per month for the 0.8 mg and 2.5 mg tablets, one bottle of 30 tablets. Read 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/foundayo, which states one hundred ninety nine dollars for the 5.5 mg strength and two hundred ninety nine dollars for the 9 mg, 14.5 mg and 17.2 mg strengths.
Zepbound, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: no published figure to $50 per month for a monthly supply, the copayment a beneficiary pays. Read 2026-10-29 at https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/weight-loss-drugs.
Wegovy injection, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: no published figure to $50 per month for a monthly supply. Read 2026-10-29 at https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/weight-loss-drugs.
Wegovy tablets, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: no published figure to $50 per month for a monthly supply. Read 2026-10-29 at https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/weight-loss-drugs.
Foundayo, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: no published figure to $50 per month for a monthly supply. Read 2026-10-29 at https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/weight-loss-drugs.

Ozempic, TrumpRx: $199 to $199, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/ozempic. The introductory terms are now read from the platform rather than reported: new self-pay patients pay this figure for the first two monthly fills of the 0.25 mg or 0.5 mg strengths, and the offer runs only between 11/17/2025 and 12/31/2026.

Zepbound, TrumpRx: $299 to $299, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/zepbound. The per-strength prices are now read from the platform: $399 for the 5 mg vial and $449 for the 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg and 15 mg vials.
Wegovy injection, starting doses, TrumpRx: $199 to $199, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/wegovy, with the introductory terms now read from the platform.
Ozempic, NovoCare self-pay: $199 to $199, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html, with the introductory terms now quoted from the manufacturer page.
Wegovy injection, starting doses, NovoCare self-pay: $199 to $199, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html, with the introductory terms now quoted from the manufacturer page.
Wegovy injection, standard doses, NovoCare self-pay: $349 to $349, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html. The Wegovy HD 7.2 mg figure is now exact at $399 per month.

Wegovy tablets, 1.5 mg, NovoCare self-pay: $149 to $149, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html. The per-strength figures are now exact: $199 for 4 mg and $299 for 9 mg and 25 mg.
Wegovy tablets, higher doses, NovoCare self-pay: $199 to $199, re-verified 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html. The 9 mg and 25 mg figures are now exact at $299 per month.

Ozempic, NovoCare savings card: no published figure to no published figure, re-checked 2026-10-29 at https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html. The manufacturer states the offer as a bound, "Pay as little as $25, subject to a maximum savings of $100/month", and a bound is not a price.

Wegovy injection, NovoCare savings card: no published figure to no published figure, re-checked 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html, which states the same bound and excludes government beneficiaries.

Ozempic, list price: no published figure to no published figure, still conflicting. Re-checked 2026-10-29: the manufacturer page states no list price, and the federal platform shows an unlabelled reference price, which does not resolve the two circulating figures.

Zepbound, list price: no published figure to no published figure, still conflicting. Re-checked 2026-10-29 at https://trumprx.gov/p/zepbound, which shows an unlabelled reference price that does not resolve the circulating manufacturer figures.

Wegovy injection, list price: no published figure to no published figure. Re-checked 2026-10-29 at https://www.novocare.com/pharmacy.html and https://trumprx.gov/p/wegovy; neither states a list price.
Wegovy tablets, list price: no published figure to no published figure. Re-checked 2026-10-29; no list price is stated for the oral product.

Medicare Part D, all six medications: no published figure to no published figure. The Part D page was read on 2026-10-29 and publishes no price for these medicines, because what a beneficiary pays depends on their own plan.
Eligibility rule, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge requires Medicare: pending primary verification to a verbatim quote from medicare.gov, read 2026-10-29.
Eligibility rule, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Part D exclusion: pending primary verification to a verbatim quote from medicare.gov, read 2026-10-29.
Eligibility rule, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge clinical criteria: the clinical criteria and the covered formulations are now quoted from medicare.gov rather than described as reported and unconfirmed.
Eligibility rule, TrumpRx manual curation: trumprx.gov is now readable, so the figures on that pathway are read from the platform rather than curated by hand.

Recorded, not promoted, 2026-10-29: the federal poverty guidelines for 2026 were read directly at https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines, so the denominator for any income threshold is now held, but the programme threshold itself remains unread and the rule stays pending.

Not read in this pass, 2026-10-29: novonordiskpap.com, which the patient-assistance rows for Ozempic and Wegovy cite, is outside the egress allowlist in docs/ops-runbook.md and was not probed; the BALANCE Model participating-state list could not be located by a static fetch of cms.gov or innovation.cms.gov.

Zepbound, TrumpRx: no published figure at any strength to $299 per month at 2.5 mg, $399 per month at 5 mg and $449 per month at 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg and 15 mg. The price was filed under the tier name "any", so a visitor who selected 15 mg was shown the 2.5 mg headline of $299; a caveat underneath an incorrect headline does not make the result accurate. The price is now filed per strength, and the higher tiers carry the 45-day refill condition the manufacturer states. Source: https://trumprx.gov/p/zepbound

Zepbound, LillyDirect self-pay: no published figure to $299 per month at 2.5 mg, $399 per month at 5 mg and $449 per month at 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg and 15 mg, read from the manufacturer self-pay terms. The higher tiers are conditional: the manufacturer states the purchase offer continues only while the refill purchase is completed within 45 days of the delivery or receipt date of the previous prescription, and that the regular price is $499 at 7.5 mg and $699 at 10 mg, 12.5 mg and 15 mg. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/zepbound/zepbound-tirzepatide-full-terms-conditions

Foundayo, list price: no published figure to $649.00 per month, read from the manufacturer price-disclosure page, whose own footnote defines the figure as the wholesale acquisition cost, accessed from AnalySource on April 3, 2026. Source: https://pricinginfo.lilly.com/foundayo

Mounjaro, list price: no published figure to $1,112.16 per fill, read from the manufacturer price-disclosure page, whose own footnote defines the figure as the wholesale acquisition cost, accessed from AnalySource on January 1, 2026. One fill is a month supply, defined by the manufacturer as four pens per month. Source: https://pricinginfo.lilly.com/mounjaro

Zepbound, list price: no published figure to no published figure. The manufacturer price-disclosure page states the list price as a range of $499 to $1,086.37 per fill. A range is a bound rather than a price, and the four circulating figures recorded before are superseded by that one authoritative statement, so no single figure is adopted. Source: https://pricinginfo.lilly.com/zepbound

Mounjaro, LillyDirect self-pay: no published figure to no published figure. The manufacturer page was read and shows the self-pay price as a starting price at every strength with no per-strength table, and a bound is not a price. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/mounjaro

Zepbound, savings card: no published figure to no published figure, re-checked against the manufacturer card terms, which state three separate bounds, each with its own savings cap and its own coverage condition, and which state that the card expires and savings end on 12/31/2026. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/zepbound/zepbound-tirzepatide-full-terms-conditions

Mounjaro, savings card: no published figure to no published figure, re-checked against the manufacturer price-disclosure page, which states the exclusion of government programmes and publishes no copay figure. Source: https://pricinginfo.lilly.com/mounjaro

Foundayo, savings card: no published figure to no published figure, re-checked against the manufacturer price-disclosure page, which states the exclusion of government beneficiaries and a bound of as little as $25. Source: https://pricinginfo.lilly.com/foundayo
Eligibility rule, manufacturer savings cards exclude federal healthcare programmes: pending primary verification to a verbatim quote from the manufacturer own savings card terms, read 2026-10-29.
Eligibility rule, manufacturer savings cards require commercial insurance: pending primary verification to a verbatim quote from the manufacturer own savings card terms, read 2026-10-29.

Correction, Zepbound, TrumpRx, 2026-10-29: the earlier note in this entry said the introductory-pricing caveat was refuted by the TrumpRx page. That was wrong, and it is replaced. The Zepbound offer is not an introductory offer at all. The manufacturer terms state a purchase offer that continues only while the refill is completed within 45 days of the previous delivery or receipt, with the regular price stated as $499 at 7.5 mg and $699 at 10 mg, 12.5 mg and 15 mg once that window is missed. The Zepbound rows now carry that precise restriction, and the TrumpRx page shows the same 45-day condition and the same contingent prices. The absence of a warning on one platform does not refute the terms on another.

Read in a browser, 2026-10-29: every Eli Lilly property refuses an automated request with HTTP 403 and a bot-protection interstitial, so the Lilly pages were read in a browser instead, which is the method docs/ops-runbook.md has always prescribed. That is how the Zepbound self-pay terms, the Zepbound savings card terms, the three price-disclosure pages and the LillyCares pages in this entry were read.

Held for 2027-01-01: the Zepbound savings card and the Zepbound KwikPen self-pay savings card both state that the card expires and savings end on 12/31/2026. That change is not applied on this branch; it is staged on mm/glp-jan1-2027.

Foundayo, LillyDirect self-pay, 0.8 mg: no published figure to $149 per month, the regular price the manufacturer states for a one-month supply. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/medicines/foundayo/foundayo-full-terms-conditions

Foundayo, LillyDirect self-pay, 2.5 mg: no published figure to $149 per month. The manufacturer states that through December 31, 2026 the self-pay price of this dose is temporarily reduced to $149 per month, and that the regular price is $199. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/medicines/foundayo/foundayo-full-terms-conditions

Foundayo, LillyDirect self-pay, mid doses: no published figure to $299 per month for the 5.5 mg and 9 mg doses, the regular price the manufacturer states for both. Through December 31, 2026 the 5.5 mg dose is temporarily reduced to $199 per month. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/medicines/foundayo/foundayo-full-terms-conditions

Foundayo, LillyDirect self-pay, top doses: conflicting to $299 per month for the 14.5 mg and 17.2 mg doses. The manufacturer states this is a purchase offer that continues only while the refill purchase is completed within 45 days of the delivery or receipt date of the previous prescription, and that the regular price for those doses is $349. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/medicines/foundayo/foundayo-full-terms-conditions

Mounjaro, LillyDirect self-pay: no published figure to $499 per month. The manufacturer page shows the same self-pay price at every strength, from 2.5 mg to 15 mg. Source: https://www.lilly.com/lillydirect/medicines/mounjaro

Eligibility rule, patient assistance income threshold: pending primary verification to a verbatim quote from the Lilly Cares eligibility page, read 2026-10-29. The programme publishes its income limits as 300%, 400% or 500% of the 2026 federal poverty guidelines, depending on the medication group.

Patient assistance, Zepbound, Mounjaro and Foundayo: the Lilly Cares medication groups were read directly on 2026-10-29 and do not include these medicines, so that programme does not cover them. The rows stay unpublished and the finding is recorded against each.

Patient assistance, Ozempic and Wegovy: the Novo Nordisk Patient Assistance Program page was read directly on 2026-10-29. It publishes the income limits, at 200% of the federal poverty level for an uninsured patient on Ozempic and 400% for any other medicine, and it states that you must have Medicare or no insurance. The rows stay unpublished because the medicine is free to a qualifying applicant and there is no price to publish. The host previously cited for these rows, novonordiskpap.com, does not resolve, and the programme now lives on novocare.com.

Ozempic, list price: still conflicting. Novo Nordisk publishes its own Ozempic price guide, and it was read on 2026-10-29: it carries the self-pay and savings prices and no list price, so the two circulating figures are still unreconciled.

title: First verified prices: NovoCare Pharmacy and TrumpRx read directly
summary: The first primary-source reads since launch. The NovoCare Pharmacy page and the federal TrumpRx platform were read directly on September 28, 2026, and eight figures were confirmed with their conditions; two insured offers were confirmed as bounds (which are not prices, so they still render no number). Every Lilly-sourced figure remains unverified because Lilly properties refuse automated readers.
changes: Confirmed on NovoCare Pharmacy: Wegovy pill self-pay tiers (starting strength, the 4 mg strength, and the two highest strengths at a higher verified figure), Wegovy injection introductory price for the two starting doses (first two monthly fills, offer verified through December 31, 2026) with the ongoing prices for standard and HD strengths, and the Ozempic introductory price with its verified ongoing prices per strength.

Confirmed on TrumpRx: the Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy pen monthly figures as displayed on the federal platform, each beside the reference figure the platform shows. The previously conflicting Zepbound figure is superseded by the current listing.
Recorded, not promoted: the insured "pay as little as" offers on NovoCare Pharmacy are verified bounds with a verified monthly savings cap, and bounds never become values under the rules of evidence.
Attempted and refused: every Lilly property refused automated readers (HTTP 403, gateway errors, timeouts), so all Lilly-sourced figures stay unverified with the attempt recorded against each.
The end-date ambiguity on the introductory offers is resolved by the direct read: the verified offer runs through December 31, 2026.

title: Site launch, with no verified prices
summary: The tool, the engine and the full source manifest go live. No price renders as a number, because on this date no figure could be confirmed against a primary source. This entry exists so the gap is on the record from day one rather than discovered later.
changes: Published the ranking engine covering 6 medications and 8 payment pathways, with eligibility rules held as data rather than prose.

Filed all 45 tracked price figures as unverified or conflicting with a null value. Outbound connections to every primary source (fda.gov, cms.gov, medicare.gov, hhs.gov, trumprx.gov, sec.gov, and all Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk domains) were refused by the network this build runs on, so none could be read directly.
Recorded, alongside each unverified figure, what research located and the provenance actually held for it, so a single verification pass can promote it without a code change.
Marked the TrumpRx pathway as manually curated: programmatic access to trumprx.gov is refused, and the November 2025 announced figures conflict with later readings of the live platform.
Excluded compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide entirely, the current lawful status being unestablished against FDA sources.
Suppressed manufacturer savings cards for Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and VA beneficiaries rather than ranking them lower, so a pathway that cannot be used is not shown as an option.
Applied the reported Medicare Bridge sleep-apnea exclusion despite being unable to confirm it, on the grounds that omitting a real exclusion would quote a price to a beneficiary who cannot obtain it.
